mission.title: openfeature: Provider lifecycle race condition in multi-threaded SDKs
mission.description: Provider lifecycle race condition in multi-threaded SDKs. Community-reported issue.

steps.title: Identify openfeature troubleshoot symptoms
steps.description:
Check for the issue in your openfeature deployment:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n openfeature -l app.kubernetes.io/name=openfeature
kubectl logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=openfeature -n openfeature --tail=100 | grep -i error
```
Look for errors or warnings in the logs that may indicate the issue.

steps.title: Review openfeature configuration
steps.description:
Inspect the relevant openfeature configuration:
```bash
kubectl get all -n openfeature -l app.kubernetes.io/name=openfeature
kubectl get configmap -n openfeature -l app.kubernetes.io/part-of=openfeature
```
I've been digging provider lifecycle in Go and Swift SDKs, and I believe there's a couple of things in OF spec that make it hard to implement it correctly in the presence of true multi-threading.

steps.title: Confirm Provider lifecycle race condition in… is resolved
steps.description:
Verify the fix by checking that the original error no longer occurs:
```bash
kubectl logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=openfeature -n openfeature --tail=50 --since=5m
kubectl get events -n openfeature --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail -10
```
Confirm that the issue symptoms are gone.
